id_west_car_body_canyon.blurb: The western wall of Car Body Canyon sits on the north side of the Boise River in the basalt Black Cliffs, a short drive from town along the Lucky Peak highway. It is mainly a trad crag with a good sport presence and one top-rope line: grades start around 5.6 and run to 5.12, with most of the climbing between 5.8 and 5.11. A brief trail leads to the base. The wall gets sun in the morning and shade later in the day, which makes it pleasant when the afternoons turn warm. Spring and autumn are generally the best seasons in the Black Cliffs, though the cliffs can be climbed through much of the year.

id_elephant_s_perch_the.blurb: A big granite face high in the Sawtooth Mountains of central Idaho, above Redfish Canyon, and the centre of the range's rock climbing. Most of what is here is long alpine-style free climbing, with some shorter trad lines and a few boulder problems at the base. The grades lean hard: the bulk fall between 5.10 and 5.11, a few reach 5.12 and 5.13, and the easiest long line tops out near 5.9 over eight pitches of cracks, chimneys, layback flakes and face moves. This is a committing mountain day rather than a quick crag visit, since the hike to the foot of the wall through the canyon is long. The stone is some of the best granite in the Sawtooths.
